answer: Summed social capital (ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument) peaked in the **14th century BCE** (1400–1301 BCE, Older Bronze Age). The peak was driven by a sharp increase in **copper/gold (ZCU_AU: −0.36 → +2.54)** and **monument count (ZMonument: +0.17 → +1.71)**, while amber (Zamber) remained near zero (−0.01) and did not contribute.

payload.hypothesis: Summed social capital (copper/gold + amber + monument count, as standardised Z-scores) peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE, Older Bronze Age). The peak was driven primarily by a sharp increase in copper/gold (Z-score −0.36 → +2.54) and monument count (+0.17 → +1.71), while amber remained near zero and did not contribute to the peak.
payload.workflow: Computed an unweighted sum of three standardised Z-scores (ZCU_AU, Zamber, ZMonument) per 100-year bin from capital.csv (endpoint convention) and cross-checked by averaging the corresponding interpolated annual series (CopperGold_inter, Amber_inter, MonumentCount_inter) within each 100-year bin from time_series_data.csv. Peak identified as the bin with maximum summed value; century number derived as BCE // 100. Both conventions agree the 14th century BCE is the peak.
